newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe announces income tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe announces income tax cuts.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Thursday that France would cut income tax by 25 billion francs ($5 billion) next year and 75 billion francs over five years in a drive to boost consumer confidence and stimulate the economy.

But in a televised statement, he said the government was extending taxation on savings to help finance the deficit-ridden welfare system. As a result the net cut in personal taxation in 1997 would be 18 billion francs.

Juppe said all income tax brackets would be lowered from next year and the top rate of income tax would fall to 54 percent from 56.8 percent. Over five years, the politically sensitive top rate would fall to 47 percent.
He also said the threshhold for paying any income tax would be raised to ease the burden on lower-income families. Half of French households already pay no income tax.
The government said it would launch private pension funds and tighten the tax treatment of life assurance policies.

The package also included the gradial elimination of special tax breaks for some 110 different professions, including journalists and airline pilots, but only from 1998, after the next general election. ($1=5.080 French Franc)
